    0.11.5 — a manifest conflict is now told to somebody
    
    boot()'s own comment said 'conflicts surfaced here'. Nothing read
    manifest.conflicts in production. mergeManifests detects two
    contributions claiming one command id, one key binding, one setting path,
    one view or one store, records who claimed each and why the loser lost --
    and six tests asserted the detection while none asserted that a running
    page ever learned of it.
    
    So the losing part's id was dropped in silence, on a page its author may
    not have composed. A green suite over an inert mechanism is worse than no
    mechanism, because it looks covered. This is the reader that makes the
    comment true and closes the sharpest entry in mesh-serve's
    spec/unread.md.
    
    A warning rather than a throw: a collision is one part losing an id, not
    a broken page, and refusing to boot because two of eight parts both
    wanted ctrl+k would take down a working desktop over a keyboard shortcut.
    The owner needs to know, which is not the same as being stopped.

Author: FLYBYME <mangoraft@gmail.com>
Date:   Sun Sep 6 01:38:43 2026 -0400

    0.11.4 — a hidden window must actually be hidden
    
    kernel.css had no [hidden] rule, and .window sets display: flex, which
    beats the user agent's [hidden] { display: none }. So every window the
    manager hid stayed on screen.
    
    In windowed mode nothing hides, which is why it went unnoticed. The first
    time it mattered was tiled mode, where visible() hides every window whose
    tile is not in the active layout: the two tiled windows laid out
    correctly at the 2:1 split their Application declared, and the other six
    floated on top of them. Tiling looked broken rather than half-applied.
    
    Third bug in one chain tonight -- setLayout never called, then the
    fallback that hid the symptom, then this. Each one hid the next.

commit dfae098cdd65b8d2f1bf2b7e4cd75fc8e84aecc1 (tag: v0.11.3)
Author: FLYBYME <mangoraft@gmail.com>
Date:   Sun Sep 6 01:36:47 2026 -0400

    0.11.3 — a declared layout now reaches the window manager
    
    setLayout was called by nothing. An Application declared layout,
    mergeManifests collected it into manifest.layouts, and
    WindowManager.setLayout existed to receive it -- three parts, no code
    joining them, so layout() was undefined for the life of every page.
    
    Tiled mode therefore had nothing to tile. The mode switched, the button's
    label changed, and not one window moved: 'the tile window button changes
    its text but the tiles do not.'
    
    manifest.layouts had zero readers in the reader audit and this is now its
    first. That audit has predicted three of tonight's bugs.
    
    The first Application with a layout wins, which is a placeholder.
    application.md section 9 says the foreground Application's layout governs
    and a background one keeps its own -- that needs the router, because what
    is foreground is a routing question. Until then a composition with one
    tiling Application behaves correctly, instead of every composition
    behaving as if none had a layout.

    0.4.0 — start(composition), so a generated page actually boots
    
    The cdn generates a page whose boot module calls start(). There was no function
    behind the call: the page loaded, the import map resolved, every part was
    fetched, and nothing happened.
    
    What it replaces is surfdns-console/src/main.ts — 140 lines, almost none of it
    about that console. A WindowManager, four settings hives and their providers,
    windowPersistence, a mesh client wired through withHeaders, a component
    registry, mountPage, an effect rendering notifications, a resize listener.
    Identical on every site, hand-written on every site, wrong differently on each.
    
    The cdn could have generated those 140 lines and must not: a generator that
    tracks another package's internals is a second copy of that package. So the
    split is the cdn generates a composition and the kernel knows how to run one.
    
    Three of the five undeclared contracts between a bundle and a hand-written page
    are gone. The kernel creates what it mounts into, mounts its own notification
    surface, and reads data-api from the document rather than being told twice. The
    import map and the stylesheet stay with the page, where they belong — they are
    what a browser needs before any of this runs.
    
    A part is a class or an instance, and accepting both is not laziness:
    extracting AuthExtension showed that a part taking site options cannot
    construct itself, so its default export has to be the constructor, and the
    kernel is the only thing holding both the class and the options.
    
    Two findings from writing the tests. kernel.start does not throw when an
    Application's start() rejects — it leaves the process failed, "a resting state,
    not a disappearance" — so a wrapper that only catches reports nothing and a
    window that never appeared is indistinguishable from one nobody asked for.
    open() reads the process table now. And a first draft of the chrome test wrote
    element('div', …); the registry refused it by name, which is the view-layer
    rule holding rather than being asked for.
